STL arrives in Minnesota with the better underlying numbers. At five on five the Blues have taken 55% of the expected goals in their games, while MIN sits at 48%. The per-60 chance creation is identical at 3.27 expected goals for, but STL gives up 2.72 against to MIN's 2.92. Special teams lean the other way: MIN's power play generates 0.60 expected goals a game against 0.43 for STL, though the Wild also take 4.14 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents power plays. The model has it close, projecting 2.62 expected goals for STL and 2.78 for MIN.

The goalie matchup favors the home side so far. Jesper Wallstedt (projected for MIN) has a .933 save percentage and is +6.83 in goals saved above expected over 6 games, after a +5.76 mark across 35 games last season. Joel Hofer (projected for STL) is at .921 and +2.47 over 4 games this year, and was +11.05 across 46 games last season, so he has the stronger track record over a larger sample.

Both teams are 2-2-1 in their last five, and the underlying results diverge. STL took more expected goals in 3 of those 5 games and averaged 55%, with its last two wins coming 5-3 over CBJ and 7-2 at OTT. MIN won the chance battle in 2 of 5 and averaged 49%, and it comes in off a 5-2 loss at WPG on Tuesday. For the model's picks, Kirill Kaprizov is the likeliest scorer on the board at 40%, with Matt Boldy at 36%. For STL, Mason McTavish leads at 25% to score and 13% for two or more points.
